propositions: An APFS RAM disk experiment was designed and implemented to reduce macOS pytest wall time by moving temporary Git repositories from runner.temp to an ephemeral mounted volume.

All treatment runs (31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, 31873067707) executed the same unchanged pytest selectors and collection counts but ran slower than the no-RAM control (17m26s default / 20m36s job), failing the predeclared retention threshold of at least 5% improvement.

The experiment exposed two test infrastructure defects: intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixtures that caused PermissionError during recursive basetemp cleanup, and a nested pytest cacheprovider leak that required explicit -p no:cacheprovider flag.

The RAM-disk lifecycle and experiment-only workflow contract were fully reverted to restore both unchanged pytest tiers to runner.temp, with selective repair only to snapshot cleanup teardown and nested pytest isolation.

All existing workflow parity, gate skew, coverage guard, and worktree pin contract tests remained unchanged and passed; selectors, markers, xdist worker counts, timeouts, platforms, and coverage behavior are identical before and after the experiment.
